title: Parse synthetic virtual-device frames

parent.objective: Demonstrate independently testable protocol components using fictional devices.
parent.milestone: Produce a deterministic parser against synthetic input fixtures.

goal: Convert synthetic byte frames into normalized readings and reject malformed frames deterministically.
non_goals: Change transport protocols or deployment settings.

allowed: Implement the fixture-only frame parser and its tests.
Document parser input and output examples.
prohibited: Edit hardware adapters, firmware, or production configuration.
Infer physical-device compatibility from these fixtures.

inputs.name: Synthetic frame specification
inputs.description: Fictional format: tag 0xA1 followed by one unsigned payload byte; all other lengths or tags are invalid.

outputs.name: Parser result
outputs.description: A reading with value 0 through 255, or a deterministic invalid-frame result.

outputs.name: Verification record
outputs.description: Sample identifiers, observed results, and test outcome for every declared fixture.

interface.name: parse_synthetic_frame
interface.description: Accept a byte sequence; return a normalized reading or invalid-frame result without side effects.

assumptions: All frame examples are synthetic and establish no real hardware behavior.

sources.reference: The fictional format and sample list embedded in this contract inputs.
sources.authority: Synthetic test specification only; not a manufacturer specification.

acceptance_criteria.description: Both valid frames produce the exact unsigned payload value.
Every listed invalid frame returns the documented error without an uncaught exception.

validation.description: Execute table-driven checks for every embedded sample.

context_scope: This contract and its embedded fictional protocol.
The isolated parser implementation and its tests.
architecture_boundaries: Keep parsing independent of transport and physical devices.
Do not change the specified input/output interface.

hardware_assumptions.assumption: A physical device would emit tag 0xA1 followed by one payload byte. The fixture asserts this; no device has been observed.
